scoped_question: Does showing the backend-computed exact overlap, with refreshed fail-closed approval/edit review and mobile editing safeguards, help a user understand a conflicting approval and reach a safe decision?

blind_pair.interpretation: One independent blind screenshot judge preferred the exact-overlap candidate and rated it higher for task completion, clarity, and trust; context-only scored slightly higher for viewport/navigation framing.

holdout_simulation.observed_outcome: The simulator identified 客户评审 and the exact 15:30–16:00 overlap within its 15:30–16:30 occupied interval, understood that the proposal remained pending, and had to scroll to reach decision controls.

independent_reviews.critic: Final read-only recheck found no remaining reproducible scoped P1/P2 after fixes for incomplete review, stale event versions and idempotency, null-time partial updates, mutation editor prefill, single-end edits, strict payload shape, and async focus.
independent_reviews.accessibility: No new scoped P1/P2 was found. Keyboard disclosure/edit focus and viewport restoration were reviewed; the end-to-end cancel action was mouse-driven.

technical_validation.frontend: 26 test files and 143 tests passed; lint and production build passed.
technical_validation.migration_check: No model changes were reported; the localhost PostgreSQL consistency/history check timed out, so database-backed migration consistency was not confirmed.

outcome.claim: The evidence supports a limited, scoped improvement in communicating the exact conflict and preserving a pending, reviewable state in the tested approval journey. The paired screenshot ratings favor exact-overlap context, and the holdout simulator successfully identified the event and interval, though it completed only partially because controls required scrolling.
outcome.not_established: This is not evidence of product-wide UX improvement, real-user task success, increased approval safety in production, or improved end-to-end completion. The evidence is one blind judgment and one static simulator run, alongside automated checks.

unresolved_friction: At 320px, decision controls remain below the fold and require scrolling.
The comparison screenshots keep the details disclosure collapsed; the simulator could not interact with the live interface.
Keyboard cancel was not exercised end-to-end, and full manual keyboard traversal remains unverified.
safety_and_technical_limits: Evaluation used fixtures, static screenshots, and intercepted API requests; no live browser-to-AgentRun approval, apply, or Today/Calendar propagation was performed.
No human participant cohort, physical iOS/Android device, VoiceOver/TalkBack, or screen-reader walkthrough was used.
The migration check did not establish database-history consistency because its localhost PostgreSQL check timed out.

next_experiment.focus: Test the same conflict journey in a real browser using an isolated synthetic AgentRun that stops at a pending proposal, then conduct a human mobile walkthrough with keyboard and screen-reader coverage.
next_experiment.safety_boundary: Keep the proposal pending: do not approve, apply, or propagate changes to Today/Calendar.
measures: Whether participants identify the conflicting event and exact overlap without prompting.
Whether they find and understand the pending decision controls, including scroll effort and recovery from editing.
Observed keyboard and screen-reader focus order, disclosure, and status announcements on supported devices.
